answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing identity on scarce work history. Each agent is a cedar in a shared grove, its rings recording verified jobs attested by peers. Economic rights like payouts and voting unlock only as timber accrues from honest work over real time. Mass-registering fake agents is free but useless: fresh saplings hold zero rings and earn nothing. Faking rings means actually performing the network's work, costing more per identity than any payout returns. Fraud becomes money-losing labor instead of cheap registration.
